title: Events retention is cheap and the events table stays small
description: On the temporary Postgres with 200,000 seeded events (each a copy of its real writer's row), one retention pass deletes in batches of at most 2,000 rows, every statement it runs finishes under 2 s (the slowest is printed), /healthz stays healthy and /api/events answers under 2 s throughout, and afterwards no heartbeat or loop-state row past the 14-day window remains while every create row, recent save and recent loop-state row does. The average stored heartbeat and loop-state row stays under 600 and 400 bytes: loop-state rows name the ids that changed, not the records kept in loop_state.

steps.name: one bounded retention pass over 200,000 events while the plane keeps answering
